html:
SMTO-EXE-0137 — That saved browser profile is already open

GUID: cd9222c9-1386-5ef5-bb5e-d650738766cc
Slug: browser-profile-in-use
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO tried to open a web browser with a saved profile, which keeps your website sign-ins between uses, but a browser using that profile is already open. Only one can use it at a time, so no new browser was opened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to keep working in the browser session that is already open with that profile. That browser already has the profile's sign-ins and pages, so nothing needs to be opened again.
  2. If another conversation opened that browser and is finished with it, go to that conversation and ask SMTO to stop its browser session. A browser belongs to the conversation that opened it, and the profile becomes free once that browser is stopped.
  3. If you don't need the saved sign-ins, ask SMTO to use a temporary browser instead of the saved profile. A temporary browser doesn't use the saved profile, so it can open alongside the other one.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the browser with that profile, or carries on in the one already open.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Restarting the Gateway closes every open browser, so they should only do it when no browser work is running. Don't delete the browser profile folder; it holds the saved sign-ins.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PlaywrightBackend._start refused a managed persistent launch because a non-ephemeral session on this Gateway already uses the requested profile ID.

What this means

  • Managed session startup found an existing non-ephemeral session using the requested profile ID and refused competing use. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Managed session startup found an existing non-ephemeral session using the requested profile ID and refused competing use.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current sessions and profile ownership before deciding whether to reuse or stop the existing session.

How to fix it

  • Find the session holding the profile (browser.sessions in the conversation that owns it) and reuse it, or stop it with browser.stop before starting the same persistent profile again; use persistence=ephemeral or a different profile for parallel work. Sessions are owned by the conversation that created them.
  • Use the existing session or stop it before starting the same persistent profile again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the existing session or stop it before starting the same persistent profile again.

How to verify the fix

  • One intended owned session uses the persistent profile without competing launch.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
